rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿjāb is pleasure in admiring what one finds pleasing; related forms describe wonder, particularly at exceptional beauty.
rows.anchor: الإعجاب هو سرور المعجب بما يستحسن ومنه العجب بالنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aladd describes one who is difficult to overcome in dispute; related ladeed can mean the two sides of a valley or anything's two sides.
rows.anchor: إذا غلبه في الخصومة ولد الدواء في حلقه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes khiṣām as the plural of khaṣm; adjectives on this pattern pluralize as fiʿāl, while nouns use afʿul in the few and fiʿāl in the many.
rows.anchor: والخصام قيل إنه جمع الخصم عن الزجاج وفعل إذا كان صفة فإنه يجمع على فعال

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl instead treats khiṣām as a verbal noun synonymous with mukhāṣama, disputation.
rows.anchor: وقيل الخصام مصدر كالمخاصمة عن الخليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawallī means turning away or moving from something toward its opposite.
rows.anchor: والتولي هو الانحراف والزوال عن الشيء إلى خلاف جهته

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Saʿā can mean to act or to hurry; al-Aʿshā's line uses it for working on behalf of Kinda.
rows.anchor:
قال الأعشى:
وسعى لكندة سعي غير مواكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasād is causing harm without entitlement or any legitimate benefit.
rows.anchor: والإفساد: هو عمل الضرر بغير استحقاق ولا وجه من وجوه المصلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihlāk removes the possibility of benefit; ḥarth means crops and nasl means offspring.
rows.anchor: والإهلاك العمل الذي ينفي الانتفاع والحرث الزرع

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk broadens the terms: ḥarth means every plant and nasl every living creature.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك الحرث كل نبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasl evokes emergence or falling away: it describes camel hair or bird feathers shedding, and humanity is Adam's progeny because people emerged from his back.
rows.anchor: ويقال نسل ينسل نسولا إذا خرج فسقط ومنه نسل وبر البعير أو ريش الطائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li-yufsida governs an implicit an, which may be made explicit; unlike 3:179, its lām is not an emphatic mark of negation.
rows.anchor: نصب بإضمار أن ويجوز إظهارها بأن يقال لأن يفسد فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the three verses were revealed about a hypocritical pretender who outwardly displays what he inwardly opposes.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس نزلت الآيات الثلاثة في المرائي

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: A report from al-Ṣādiq also identifies the verses' referent as a particular person, without naming him here.
rows.anchor: وهو المروي عن الصادق ع إلا أنه عين المعني به

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the verses were revealed about the hypocrites generally.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: نزلت في المنافقين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the referent as al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, who displayed affection for the Prophet and Islam while concealing the opposite.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق وكان يظهر الجميل بالنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage turns from the previously described believers and unbelievers to the condition of hypocrites.
rows.anchor: ثم بين سبحانه حال المنافقين بعد ذكره أحوال المؤمنين والكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrite's speech pleases Muhammad and makes a strong impression.
rows.anchor: أي تستحسن كلامه يا محمد ويعظم موقعه من قلبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says that he believes in Muhammad and is his companion, or makes similar claims.
rows.anchor: أي يقول آمنت بك وأنا صاحب لك ونحو ذلك

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls God to witness that his words reflect his heart, although his heart actually contradicts them.
rows.anchor: أي يحلف بالله ويشهده على أنه مضمر ما يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is the most relentless of disputants; if khiṣām is a verbal noun, the phrase means a fierce, false arguer.
rows.anchor: وهو أشد المخاصمين خصومة ومن قال إن الخصام مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that he turns away from what is good.
rows.anchor: أي أعرض عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes tawallā as gaining authority and becoming a governor.
rows.anchor: ملك الأمر وصار واليا عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj takes it as turning away from the promise he had made in his speech.
rows.anchor: ولي عن قوله الذي أعطاه عن أبن جريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He hurries away from Muhammad, or the phrase means that he works on earth.
rows.anchor: أي أسرع في المشي من عندك وقيل عمل في الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains the corruption as severing kinship and spilling blood.
rows.anchor: ليقطع الرحم ويسفك الدماء عن ابن جريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that he spreads corruption and commits acts of disobedience.
rows.anchor: ليظهر الفساد ويعمل المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened destruction is of crops and children.
rows.anchor: أي النبات والأولاد وذكر الأزهري أن الحرث النساء

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azharī says ḥarth can mean women and nasl their children, connecting the image to 2:223.
rows.anchor: وذكر الأزهري أن الحرث النساء والنسل الأولاد لقوله

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: The verse 2:223 calls wives a field, supporting al-Azharī's gloss of ḥarth as women.
rows.anchor: نساؤكم حرث لكم [البقرة: 223] وروي عن الصادق ع

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq interprets ḥarth here as religion and nasl as people.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الصادق ع إن الحرث في الموضع الذين والنسل الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejected corruption may mean corrupt action or, in another explanation, corrupt people.
rows.anchor: أي العمل بالفساد وقيل أهل الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the Mujabbira: God's love is His will, so His denial of love for corruption means He does not will corruption.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على بطلان قول المجبرة إن الله تعالى يريد القبائح لأنه تعالى نفى عن نفسه محبة الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittiqāʾ is seeking safety through what protects from danger; fearing God means guarding against His punishment.
rows.anchor: الاتقاء طلب السلامة بما يحجز عن المخافة واتقاء الله إنما هو اتقاء عذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhdh is the opposite of giving; ʿizza is strength that keeps one from humiliation.
rows.anchor: والأخذ ضد الإعطاء والعزة القوة التي تمتنع بها عن الذلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mihād is a bed or resting place; anything trodden or used as a bed has been prepared as a resting place.
rows.anchor: والمهاد الوطاء من كل شيء وكل شيء وطئته فقد مهدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrite is told to stop his campaign of corruption and destruction of crops and offspring.
rows.anchor: وإذا قيل لهذا المنافق اتق الله فيما نهاك عنه من السعي في الأرض بالفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that pride and tribal zeal drive him into sin, as something taking hold can compel or bind a person.
rows.anchor: حملته العزة وحمية الجاهلية على فعل الإثم ودعته إليه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains that pride seized him because of the unbelief already in his heart.
rows.anchor: أخذته العزة من أجل الإثم الذي في قلبه من الكفر عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is a sufficient punishment for his leading others astray.
rows.anchor: فكفاه عقوبة من إضلاله أن يصلى نار جهنم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses mihād as a settled abode; a resting place suggests permanence beneath its occupant.
rows.anchor: أي القرار عن الحسن كما قال في موضع آخر وبئس القرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation calls Hell a mihād by substitution for the promised resting place, paralleling the reversed glad tidings in 31:7.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنما سميت جهنم مهادا لأنها بدل من المهاد كما قال سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arrogantly refusing truth when admonished is an enormous sin; Ibn Masʿūd says an unforgiven sin is telling a man to fear God and hearing him retort, You mind yourself.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن من تكبر عن قبول الحق إذا دعي إليه كان مرتكبا أعظم كبيرة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says a grave unforgiven sin is for a man told to fear God to answer, You mind yourself.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود إن من الذنوب التي لا تغفر أن يقال للرجل اتق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurūʾ has the few plural aqruʾ and the more commonly used aqraʾ or qurūʾ; the common plural form signals the many women governed by the rule although each waits three periods.
rows.anchor: القروء جمع قرء وجمعه القليل أقرء والكثير أقراء وقروء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One root sense of qurʾ is gathering, as with the gathering of letters in recitation or a womb gathering around a pregnancy.
rows.anchor: وأصله في اللغة يحتمل وجهين

rows.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm's line uses qaraʾ for a womb that has not gathered a fetus, illustrating the root sense of gathering.
rows.anchor:
قال عمرو بن كلثوم:
ذراعي عيطل أدماء بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the gathering sense, a woman is said to have aqraʾ when she menstruates as blood gathers in the womb; qurʾ can also mean purity as blood gathers in the body.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا يقال أقرأت المرأة فهي مقرىء إذا حاضت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second root sense is a regularly recurring time, which can designate either menstruation or purity.
rows.anchor: والوجه الثاني: إن أصل القرء الوقت الجاري في الفعل على عادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet's line about the time when winds blow illustrates the sense of a regularly recurring time.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
شنئت العقر عقر بني شليل

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā's lines about his wives' qurūʾ use the term for periods of purity, supporting that interpretation.
rows.anchor:
قول الأعشى:
وفي كل عام أنت جاشم غزوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿūla is the plural of baʿl, husband; the husband is called this because he is above the woman through marital authority.
rows.anchor: والبعولة جمع بعل ويقال بعل يبعل بعولة وهو بعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 37:125 baʿl means a lord or, alternatively, an idol; baʿl also names a palm watered by its roots.
rows.anchor: [الصافات: 125] أي ربا وقيل أنه صنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Related uses describe being constricted by a matter, acting arrogantly, or a bewildered woman; the root's underlying idea is superiority.
rows.anchor: وبعل الرجل بأمره إذا ضاق به ذراعا لأنه علاه منه ما ضاق به ذرعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijāl and related forms derive from strength; daraja means rank or degree.
rows.anchor: الرجال جمع رجل يقال رجل بين الرجلة أي القوة

words: إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional answer is omitted: if they believe, they will not conceal; the answer to the husbands' condition is likewise omitted and understood as their being entitled to return them.
rows.anchor: إن كن يؤمن بالله } جواب الشرط محذوف وتقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The annexation in mithlu alladhī ʿalayhinna is not a true genitive construction because alladhī ʿalayhinna functions as its object.
rows.anchor: مثل الذي عليهن إضافة مثل غير حقيقية لأن الذي عليهن مفعوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waiting-period rule concerns divorced women who have consummated marriage, menstruate, and are not pregnant; they wait until three qurūʾ pass and may not marry meanwhile.
rows.anchor: يعني المطلقات المدخول بهن من ذوات الحيض غير الحوامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is grammatically declarative but functions as a command to wait.
rows.anchor: ينتظرن بأنفسهن انقضاء ثلاثة قروء فلا يتزوجن لفظه خبر ومعناه أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author and the Imāmī position take qurūʾ as periods of purity; this is also attributed to Zayd ibn Thābit, ʿĀʾisha, Ibn ʿUmar, Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and the people of Medina.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالقروء الأطهار عندنا، وبه قال زيد بن ثابت

rows.speaker: ابن شهاب
rows.claim: Ibn Shihāb says all the people of his region held that the aqrāʾ are periods of purity except Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib.
rows.anchor: قال ابن شهاب: ما رأيت أحدا من أهل بلدنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The competing view takes qurūʾ as menstruations, attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, and also reported from ʿAlī; it is Abū Ḥanīfa's position.
rows.anchor: والمروي عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود والحسن ومجاهد ورووه أيضا عن علي أن القرء الحيض

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and his followers support the menstruation interpretation with a report that the Prophet told a woman to stop praying during her days of qurūʾ.
rows.anchor: وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة وأصحابه واستشهدوا بقوله عليه السلام للمستحاضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited instruction to a mustaḥāḍa to stop praying on her qurūʾ days supports the menstruation interpretation, since prayer is suspended during menstruation.
rows.anchor: والصلاة إنما تترك في أيام الحيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the purity interpretation, the author cites 65:1, understood as ordering divorce during a pure period in which the couple has not had intercourse.
rows.anchor: أي في طهر لم تجامع فيه كما يقال لغرة الشهر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When Ibn ʿUmar divorced his wife during menstruation, the Prophet told him to take her back and, once she was pure, either divorce or keep her.
rows.anchor: ويقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما طلق ابن عمر زوجته وهي حائض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's recitation of 65:1 indicates that the waiting period begins with purity: a woman divorced during menstruation has not yet begun it.
rows.anchor: فأخبر أن العدة الأطهار دون الحيض لأنها حينئذ تستقبل عدتها

rows.speaker: ربيعة الرأي
rows.claim: Rabīʿa al-Raʾy says the Qurʾānic aqrāʾ are the periods of purity between menstruations, not menstruations themselves.
rows.anchor: وروى أصحابنا عن زرارة قال: سمعت ربيعة الرأي يقول

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Bāqir says Rabīʿa did not reach the view independently but received it from ʿAlī.
rows.anchor: قال فدخلت على أبي جعفر فحدثته بما قال ربيعة فقال: كذب

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī says qurʾ is purity: blood gathers during that period and is expelled when menstruation comes; the waiting period ends upon entering the third menstruation.
rows.anchor: قال: نعم. كان يقول إنما القرء الطهر تقرأ فيه الدم

rows.speaker: الباقر
rows.claim: Al-Bāqir rejects the Iraqi report that ʿAlī said a husband retains the right of return until the third menstruation has ended.
rows.anchor: إن أهل العراق يروون عن علي ع أنه كان يقول هو أحق بردها

words: أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ
rows.speaker: إبراهيم وعكرمة
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm and ʿIkrima take what is hidden in the wombs to mean menstruation.
rows.anchor: قيل أراد به الحيض عن إبراهيم وعكرمة

words: أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda take it to mean pregnancy.
rows.anchor: وقيل أراد به الحبل عن ابن عباس وقتادة

words: أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ
rows.speaker: ابن عمر والحسن والصادق
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ṣādiq include both menstruation and pregnancy; the author prefers this broader interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقيل أراد به الحيض والحبل عن ابن عمر والحسن وهو المروي عن الصادق ع

words: أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ
rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says God entrusted women with three matters: menstruation, purity, and pregnancy.
rows.anchor: قال قد فوض الله إلى النساء ثلاثة أشياء الحيض والطهر والحمل

words: أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says concealment would wrong the husband by preventing him from returning to his wife.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يحل لهن الكتمان لئلا يظلمن الزوج بمنع المراجعة عن ابن عباس

words: أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says concealment could falsely attribute a child to someone else, as in pre-Islamic practice.
rows.anchor: وقيل بنسبة الولد إلى غيره كفعل الجاهلية عن قتادة

words: إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faith clause is not a legal condition permitting unbelievers to conceal; it warns that true faith prevents this sin.
rows.anchor: وليس هذا بشرط حتى أنها إذا لم تكن مؤمنة يحل لها الكتمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: While the waiting period remains, husbands may restore their wives to the prior marital state; that right expires when the period ends.
rows.anchor: يعني إن أزواجهن أولى بمراجعتهن وهي ردهن إلى الحالة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A husband alone may revoke a revocable divorce without his wife's consent, a new contract, or witnesses; the right applies only to revocable divorces although the opening is general.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا ما يدل على أن الزوج ينفرد بالمراجعة ولا يحتاج في ذلك إلى رضاء المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Men used to divorce once, wait until the period nearly ended, revoke, and repeat the cycle before divorcing a third time, thereby harming the wife.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الرجل كان إذا أراد الإضرار بامرأته طلقها واحدة وتركها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revocation is permitted for reconciliation rather than harm, but this condition concerns permissibility, not legal effect; the community agrees the legal effects still apply when harm is intended.
rows.anchor: وإنما شرط الإصلاح في إباحة الرجعة لا في ثبوت أحكامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This concise principle gives women rights corresponding to their obligations, governed by accepted standards of decent treatment.
rows.anchor: وهذا من الكلمات العجيبة الجامعة للفوائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women's rights include good companionship, freedom from harm, equitable division, maintenance, and clothing; the husband's include obedience, marital exclusivity, and preserving his paternity.
rows.anchor: كما أن للزوج حقوقا عليها مثل الطاعة التي أوجبها الله عليها له

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report prompted by a woman identified as Muʿādh's wife says a husband must not strike his wife's face or insult her, and must feed and clothe her as he does himself and not abandon her.
rows.anchor: يا رسول الله ما حق الزوجة على زوجها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet reminds men that they received women in God's trust; wives must preserve marital exclusivity, and husbands owe them customary maintenance and clothing, with any corrective strike non-injurious.
rows.anchor: وروي عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda say men's degree includes women's obedience, men's authority to dissolve the marriage, a larger inheritance share, and jihad.
rows.anchor: زيادة الميراث على قسم المرأة والجهاد هذا قول مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the degree as a man's obligation to show extra generosity and not demand every right in full.
rows.anchor: جميع حقي ليكون لي عليها الفضيلة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says women receive pleasure from men as men receive it from women, while men have a degree through spending and care.
rows.anchor: وله الفضل بنفقته وقيامه عليها عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm's tafsir says men's rights over women are greater than women's rights over men.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم قال: حق الرجال على النساء أفضل

rows.speaker: الباقر
rows.claim: A report from al-Bāqir says a wife should obey her husband, seek permission for household charity, voluntary fasting, and leaving home, and not deny him sex; the husband's right is paramount, and the Prophet says he would have ordered prostration to him if it were permitted.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب من لا يحضره الفقيه روي عن الباقر ع قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is powerful over whatever He wills, cannot be prevented or overcome, and acts according to wisdom.
rows.anchor: أي قادر على ما يشاء يمنع ولا يمنع ويقهر ولا يقهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the rule is abrogated for a woman divorced before consummation and for a pregnant divorcee by 33:49 and 65:4.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل في الآية إن المطلقة قبل الدخول والمطلقة الحاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view treats those two cases as specified exceptions to this verse rather than abrogated portions.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهما مخصوصتان من الآية كما ذكرناه في أول الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijālan is the plural of rāجل, one who is on foot, standing or walking; rukbān is the plural of rāكب, one who rides or is mounted.
rows.anchor: الرجال جمع راجل مثل تجار وصحاب وقيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of riding means to mount or be above something; rikāb can mean riding camels, and the root extends to striking a body part with one's knee.
rows.anchor: وكل شيء علا شيئا فقد ركبه والركاب المطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijālan is an accusative circumstantial expression with an implied command: pray on foot.
rows.anchor: رجالا منصوب على الحال تقديره فصلوا رجالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf in kamā is attached to udhkurū, mā is a verbal noun, and mā lam takūnū taʿlamūn is a relative clause serving as the second object of ʿallama.
rows.anchor: كما علمكم الكاف يتعلق باذكروا وما مصدرية في ما علمكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing the duty to maintain prayer, the passage gives a concession for circumstances of fear.
rows.anchor: لما قدم سبحانه وجوب المحافطة على الصلاة عقبه بذكر الرخصة عند المخافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear here is danger that prevents worshippers from standing in devotion and fulfilling prayer properly.
rows.anchor: أي إن لم يمكنكم أن تقوموا قانتين موفين الصلاة حقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In fear, pray on foot or walking, or mounted on the backs of animals; this refers to the fear prayer against an enemy.
rows.anchor: أي فصلوا رجالا على أرجلكم وقيل مشاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fear prayer consists of two rakʿas in travel and residence, except for the three-rakʿa Maghrib prayer.
rows.anchor: وصلاة الخوف من العدو ركعتان في السفر والحضر إلا المغرب فإنها ثلاث ركعات

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: It is reported that ʿAlī prayed five prayers on the night of al-Harīr by gestures, or, in another report, by takbīr.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن عليا صلى ليلة الهرير خمس صلوات بالإيماء وقيل بالتكبير

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed by gestures on the day of the Battle of the Trench.
rows.anchor: وإن النبي صلى يوم الأحزاب إيماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When danger has passed, one explanation is to perform the normal prayer; another is to remember God with praise and thanksgiving.
rows.anchor: أي فصلوا صلاة الأمن وقيل اذكروا الله بالثناء عليه

words: كَمَا عَلَّمَكُم مَّا لَمْ تَكُونُوا۟ تَعْلَمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught them matters of religion as well as other matters they had not known.
rows.anchor: من أمور دينكم وغير ذلك من أموركم

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وأبو جعفر ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, Abū Jaʿfar, and Yaʿqūb read yaghfiru and yuʿadhdhibu with indicative endings; the other readers read both in the jussive.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وعاصم وأبو جعفر ويعقوب فيغفر ويعذب بالرفع

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī prefers the jussive because it coordinates with the preceding wording and preserves its verbal pattern.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: وجه قول من جزم أنه اتبعه ما قبله

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The indicative reading separates the verbs either as a predicate of an omitted subject or as a new verbal clause coordinated with what precedes.
rows.anchor: ومن لم يجزم قطعة من الأول وقطعة منه على أحد وجهين

words: لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ownership lām means God controls and governs the heavens, earth, and all within them by His power and because He created them.
rows.anchor: اللام لام الملك أي له تصريف السموات والأرض وما فيهما

words: وَإِن تُبْدُوا مَا فِي أَنفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people reveal or hide includes obedience and disobedience; God knows it and recompenses them.
rows.anchor: أي تظهروا ما في أنفسكم من الطاعة والمعصية

words: وَإِن تُبْدُوا مَا فِي أَنفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others explain the passage as revealing or concealing testimony, which God knows and recompenses.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه إن تظهروا الشهادة أو تكتموها فإن الله يعلم ذلك

words: وَإِن تُبْدُوا مَا فِي أَنفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the statement generally across the legal rulings previously mentioned in the sūra, warning against acting contrary to them.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنها عامة في الأحكام التي تقدم ذكرها في السورة

words: وَإِن تُبْدُوا مَا فِي أَنفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some call the verse abrogated by 2:286, but the author rejects this as based on a weak report: impossible burdens cannot be imposed or abrogated, and the verse concerns accountable beliefs and intentions, not involuntary thoughts.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يصح لأن تكليف ما ليس في الوسع غير جائز

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wusʿ is less than ṭāqa: capacity is what a person can bear without being constrained; akhṭaʾnā means committing an error or sin.
rows.anchor: الوسع ما دون الطاقة ويسمى ذلك وسعا بمعنى أنه يسع الإنسان

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says akhṭaʾa and khaṭiʾa are both Arabic forms, but the former can be sinful or non-sinful error while the latter means sin alone.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة أخطأ وخطئ لغتان والفرق بين أخطأ وخطئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses khaṭiʾū for sinning against what is right, witnessing the sin-specific sense of khaṭiʾa.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
والناس يلحون الأمير إذا هم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṣr means weight or burden; it can also denote a binding covenant or kinship tie.
rows.anchor: والأصر في اللغة الثقل قال النابغة

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha's poetry uses iṣr for the burden of protecting one's people from oppression.
rows.anchor:
قال النابغة:
يا مانع الضيم أن يغشى سراتهم

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha also uses iṣr to mean a covenant or binding promise.
rows.anchor: والإسلام الإصر قال النابغة

rows.speaker: الكميت
rows.claim: Al-Kumayt's verse uses āṣirat al-arḥām for the bond of kinship.
rows.anchor:
قال الكميت:
نضحت أديم الود بيني وبينهم

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands or forbids only what a person can do; another explanation says He requires ease rather than hardship and does not exhaust capacity.
rows.anchor: لا يأمر ولا ينهى أحدا إلا ما هو له مستطيع

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna calls it a good interpretation that God does not impose a person's full limit of capacity, which would exhaust their effort.
rows.anchor: عن سفيان بن عيينة وهذا قول حسن

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse disproves the Mujabbira's allowance of obligations beyond ability: capacity lies within human power, beyond which effort is exhausted.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على بطلان قول المجبرة في تجويز تكليف العبد ما لا يطيقه

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative that wusʿ means only what is permitted is mistaken: it makes the command circular, since every command itself permits the commanded act.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن معناه إلا ما يسعها ويحل لها وهذا خطأ

words: لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person receives the reward of obedience and bears the consequence of sins; both may be called earnings because they result from one's acts.
rows.anchor: معناه لها ثواب ما كسبت من الطاعات

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan understands the prayer as an instruction to say these words, teaching believers how to supplicate.
rows.anchor: قيل تقديره قولوا ربنا على جهة التعليم للدعاء عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading supplies they say, presenting the words as reported praise and supplication.
rows.anchor: وقيل تقديره يقولون ربنا على جهة الحكاية والثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes forgetting as abandoning obedience and error as committing sins, even deliberately; the prayer seeks forgiveness for neglected duties and wrongful acts.
rows.anchor: أي تركوا طاعته فتركهم من ثوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites 9:67 and 2:44 for nasiya meaning abandonment, and an unnamed poet who uses nāsiyan for leaving off spear thrusts in battle.
rows.anchor:
ومنه قول الشاعر:
ولم أك عند الجود للجود قاليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading asks pardon if people expose themselves to circumstances that cause forgetfulness or error about a command or duty.
rows.anchor: أن معنى قوله إن نسينا أن تعرضنا لأسباب يقع عندها النسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading means accidentally failing an obligation or unintentionally doing a forbidden act; the plea expresses humility even though such acts are not punished.
rows.anchor: لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أي إن لم نفعل فعلا يجب فعله على سبيل السهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This humble appeal resembles the following plea not to impose what people cannot bear, which may also be devotional.
rows.anchor: ويجري ذلك مجرى قوله فيما بعد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAṭāʾ understand it as asking not to be punished for disobedience, whether done in ignorance or deliberately.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن ابن عباس وعطاء أن معناه لا تعاقبنا إن عصينا جاهلين أو متعمدين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والربيع والسدي
rows.claim: One explanation asks God not to impose a duty people cannot carry out or punish them for abandoning or violating it.
rows.anchor: لا تحمل علينا عملا نعجز عن القيام به ولا تعذبنا بتركه ونقضه

rows.speaker: الربيع ومالك وعطاء
rows.claim: A second explanation, reported from al-Rabīʿ, Mālik, and ʿAṭāʾ, asks God not to make the religious burden too heavy or strict.
rows.anchor: لا تحمل علينا ثقلا عن الربيع ومالك وعطاء يعني لا تشدد الأمر علينا

words: كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier communities were punished for sins, had lawful foods forbidden, and received heavier covenants and obligations; this community's lighter burden is a mercy.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا إذا ارتكبوا خطيئة عليهم عقوبتها وحرم عليهم بسببها ما أحل لهم من الطعام

words: كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on good foods for the earlier community is illustrated by 4:160, which says they were forbidden lawful good things because of wrongdoing.
rows.anchor:
كما قال تعالى
فبظلم من الذين هادوا

words: وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation asks not to be burdened with crushing duties or trials, such as killing oneself as repentance for sin.
rows.anchor: أن معناه ما يثقل علينا تحمله من أنواع التكاليف والامتحان

words: وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation asks protection from punishment that people cannot endure in this life or the next.
rows.anchor: والثاني: بمعناه ما لا طاقة لنا به من العذاب عاجلا وآجلا

words: وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation treats this as devotional petition, though God does not impose on anyone a burden beyond their capacity.
rows.anchor: والثالث: أنه على سبيل التعبد وإن كان تعالى لا يكلف ولا يحمل أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks God to pardon sins, cover errors, and show mercy through blessing in this world, pardon in the next, and admission to Paradise.
rows.anchor: ذنوبنا { واغفر لنا } خطايانا أي استرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawlānā means our protector, the one entitled to direct our affairs, and our helper.
rows.anchor: أي ولينا وأولى بالتصرف فينا وناصرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final plea asks God to help believers overcome unbelievers by force and by the strength of their argument.
rows.anchor: أي أعنا عليهم بالقهر لهم والغلبة بالحجة عليهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says that at every section of this supplication God answers, I have done so and granted it.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A well-known Prophetic report says whoever recites the final two verses of al-Baqara at night is sufficed for that night's vigil.
rows.anchor: ففي الحديث المشهور عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that during the Night Journey the Prophet reached the Lote Tree, received the five prayers and the final verses of al-Baqara, and his community's monotheists were forgiven except for grave sins.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن مسعود قال:

rows.speaker: ابن المنكدر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munkadir transmits from the Prophet that the final verses of al-Baqara are Qur'an and supplication and please the Merciful.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن المنكدر رفعه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In al-Kalbī's tafsir report from Ibn ʿAbbās, an angel announces two lights not given to a prophet before—the Opening and the end of al-Baqara—and says reciters will receive their request.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير الكلبي بإسناده ذكره عن ابن عباس قال بينا رسول الله إذ سمع نقيضا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says that when a man learned Sūrat al-Baqara, he became earnest and respected among the community.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عبد الله بن مسعود أنه قال: كان الرجل إذا تعلم سورة البقرة
